title: Arsenal Player Ratings vs. Lille: Rotated Gunners Extend Brilliant League Phase Record
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack5:12 PM EDTArsenal eventually cruised to another Champions League victory at the Emirates. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesArsenal’s outstanding Champions League home record under Mikel Arteta continued on Tuesday evening, as three second-half goals saw the Gunners ease past Lille 3–0.
Arteta’s men thus followed up their victory in Naples with another triumph, as they aim to avoid two extra matches in the new year by finishing inside the top eight of the league phase table.

Lille had been relatively comfortable in the opening hour, with a varied approach in possession limiting the damage a rotated Arsenal could inflict with their press. However, the Gunners slowly turned the screw after an uninspired first half, and Jurriën Timber’s smart finish proved to be the spark a frustrated Emirates crowd sorely needed.

Arteta subsequently pivoted to Bukayo Saka and Martin Ødegaard as part of a triple-change, and the former teed up Eberechi Eze for Arsenal’s second almost immediately after his introduction. Saka then got on the scoresheet himself as the hosts threatened a walkover, but Lille were at least able to prevent Arsenal from running up the score in the closing stages.

Arsenal are far better when Viktor Gyökeres isn’t on the field. / John Walton/PA Images/Getty Images“The happiest thing, the thing we can do to be the happiest, is to win football matches. That’s the best medicine for everybody,” Arteta asserted in the build-up to Lille’s visit, explaining how the Gunners will overcome their heartbreak in Budapest.

There has been only one blip in Arsenal’s season to date, but the boss cannot be overly pleased with his side’s level of performance on either side of the extended international break. At the moment, the Gunners are delivering in spurts, but that’s been enough in back-to-back games.

Once again, those in reserve huffed and puffed their way through proceedings, struggling to assert themselves in the contest and hardly instilling fear in those above them in the pecking order. Viktor Gyökeres was anonymous, and we can’t exactly say the Swede is desperate for a goal. He scored four for his country during the recent break.

Timber’s strike broke the shackles and forced a relatively comfortable but increasingly frail Lille, boasting the joint-best defensive record in Ligue 1, to change tack slightly. However, the visitors ultimately succumbed to a Gunners outfit that drastically improved once Arteta made changes that were planned before Timber’s opener.

From then on, it was a familiar Champions League night for the Emirates faithful since Arteta guided the club back into Europe’s premier club competition three years ago. Still, the Spaniard won’t be overly thrilled with the level shown by a tinkered attack for an hour.
Gabriel faced off against his former club. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: David Raya—6.7: Rarely is Arsenal’s No. 1 tested on such occasions, and it was more of the same here.
RB: Jurrïen Timber—8.6: Timber was keen to contribute going forward all night, and his perseverance paid off by opening the scoring with a cultured touch and finish.
CB: Ezri Konsa—7.4: A night of few issues for Konsa, who wasn’t tested by an imbalanced and lightweight Lille attack.

CB: Gabriel—6.7: Gabriel made a superb block to deny Dilane Bakwa early on, and it seemed as if Arsenal would at least be put to the test by the visitors in transition. However, that was as good as it got for Ancelotti’s side.

LB: Myles Lewis-Skelly—7.8: Back to where it all began in the senior team, Lewis-Skelly wasn’t troubled all that much despite Bakwa’s bright start, and he was a threat in the final third toward the end of the first half.
CM: Declan Rice—7.7: Nothing spectacular from Arsenal’s captain on the night, who went about his work without fuss.
CM: Bruno Guimarães—8.2: Probed unrelentingly, especially at the start of the second half, and he looked like making something happen. Had a couple of shots on goal, too.

RW: Noni Madueke—7.8: Offered plenty of threat and dominated his duel one-on-one with former Southampton defender Romain Perraud. The combination with Timber eventually bore fruit, but he’d be much better off if he looked up before he delivered into the box.
AM: Mikel Merino—6.6: Merino earned a rare start, but he was no Martin Ødegaard. The Spaniard offers something completely different, and he should’ve headed Arsenal into a first-half lead.
